p: The beauty of Hoo Zoo is that it caters for two very different moods in one ticket. Animal lovers can take things slowly with the creatures, while the dino fans are itching to get to the trail. A good plan is to do the animals first while everyone is fresh, then save the dinosaurs as the big finale. That gives you something to dangle in front of a flagging five-year-old, and it means the most exciting bit comes last. A camera is a must for the classic photo of a small child being menaced by a giant set of jaws.

Kids who are into dinosaurs often love a bit of science too, so pack some questions to spark conversation on the walk round. How big was it? What did it eat? Would it fit in our garden? It turns a fun day into a sneaky learning one without anyone noticing.

Telford is a brilliant base for a longer stay. The Ironbridge Gorge has a whole family of museums, and Blists Hill Victorian Town is a particular favourite, where you can wander streets set in Victorian times, chat to costumed townsfolk and swap modern money for old coins to spend in the shops. The famous Iron Bridge itself, the first in the world made from cast iron, spans the Severn just down the road. If you'd rather have a hill and a view, The Wrekin rises up to the west of Telford and is a popular walk with sweeping views across Shropshire on a clear day. Shrewsbury, with its medieval streets and riverside, is also an easy drive away.
